subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Feudalism was a system based on:
options: Land granted in return for service and loyalty
questions.explain: In feudalism, lords granted land (fiefs) in exchange for military service and obligations.

questions.q: In the manorial system, serfs were:
questions.explain: Serfs were unfree peasants tied to the manor, owing labour and dues to the lord.

questions.q: The Silk Road primarily facilitated:
options: Long-distance trade and exchange between East and West
questions.explain: The Silk Road carried goods, ideas and technologies across Eurasia.

questions.q: Guilds in medieval towns functioned to:
options: Collect the salt tax in India
questions.explain: Guilds controlled standards, prices and apprenticeships within a craft or trade.

questions.q: The Black Death of the mid-14th century caused:
options: The founding of the Roman Empire
questions.explain: The Black Death killed a large share of the population across Afro-Eurasia.

questions.q: A major economic consequence of the Black Death in Europe was:
options: Labour shortages and, over time, the decline of serfdom
questions.explain: Population loss raised the value of labour, weakening serfdom and shifting economic power.

questions.q: The medieval Catholic Church in Europe was:
options: A dominant religious, social and political institution
questions.explain: The Church shaped belief, learning, landholding and politics across medieval Europe.

questions.q: The Islamic Golden Age (notably under the Abbasids) was known for:
options: Advances in science, medicine and scholarship
questions.explain: Scholars in the Islamic world made major contributions in mathematics, medicine and philosophy.

questions.q: Song dynasty China (960-1279) experienced:
options: Commercial growth, urbanisation and the use of paper money
questions.explain: Song China saw notable commercialisation, technological innovation and urban growth.

questions.q: Trans-Saharan trade routes carried goods such as:
questions.explain: West African empires traded gold and salt across the Sahara.

questions.q: Mansa Musa was a famous ruler of:
questions.explain: Mansa Musa, ruler of Mali, was renowned for his wealth and famous pilgrimage to Mecca.

questions.q: In medieval Europe, monasteries served as:
options: Centres of learning, worship and agriculture
questions.explain: Monasteries preserved learning, copied manuscripts and managed farmland.

questions.q: The adoption of the three-field system in medieval agriculture:
options: Improved productivity by rotating crops and leaving land fallow
questions.explain: Three-field rotation increased yields compared with earlier two-field methods.

questions.q: In feudal society, the social hierarchy was typically topped by:
questions.explain: Feudal hierarchy placed the monarch and great nobles above knights, then peasants.

questions.q: Medieval towns grew largely because of:
options: The revival of trade and commerce
questions.explain: Expanding trade encouraged the growth of towns and a money economy.

questions.q: The Crusades (11th-13th centuries) affected the medieval world by:
options: Increasing contact and trade between Europe and the Middle East
questions.explain: Beyond warfare, the Crusades stimulated exchange of goods, ideas and technologies.

questions.q: The Indian Ocean trade network linked:
options: East Africa, Arabia, India and Southeast Asia
questions.explain: Monsoon-driven maritime trade connected diverse regions around the Indian Ocean.

questions.q: A 'fief' in the feudal system was:
options: Land granted by a lord in return for service
questions.explain: A fief was the landholding granted to a vassal in exchange for obligations.

questions.q: Comparing the medieval European and Islamic economies of this period is an example of:
questions.explain: Comparing societies and economies across regions is a central IB historical skill.

questions.q: Over the period 750-1400, the growth of long-distance trade illustrates the historical concept of:
questions.explain: Tracing how trade and economies changed (and persisted) over centuries reflects change and continuity.

specSource: IB Diploma History guide (first assessment 2020); World history topics (Paper 2): Society and economy (750-1400)
